newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: NO BIDDERS SHOW FOR S.KOREA HANBO STEEL AUCTION.
newsitem.headline: NO BIDDERS SHOW FOR S.KOREA HANBO STEEL AUCTION.

text.p: South Korean creditor banks failed on Tuesday in their third attempt to auction off Hanbo Steel Co when no bidders showed up, main creditor Korea First Bank said in a statement.
The next step would be private negotiations with possible buyers, the statement said.
Creditors said they would formally announce on Thursday their intention to sell the failed steelmaker through private negotiations.
Potential buyers would have until August 21 to submit an application to creditors, the statement said.
If no acceptable buyer was found through private negotiations, creditors would submit all offers to a special committee which would decide how to dispose of Hanbo, the statement said.
The only offer for Hanbo so far was from Pohang Iron and Steel Co (POSCO) which last month jointly proposed with Dong Kuk Steel Mill to buy Hanbo's assets for two trillion won.
The latest official evaluation of Hanbo put the company's fixed assets at 4.15 trillion won. Hanbo creditors rejected POSCO's proposal at the second auction as too low.

After the third auction failed, a Korea First official told reporters creditors would consider POSCO's proposal if they were unable to sell Hanbo through private negotiations. "We still think POSCO's offered money is unsatisfactory," he said.
